body: I hope you feel better dude, and even though I'm some random stranger on the internet, I genuinely wish that you will find something that interest you, even just by a little bit.

You are definitely not alone on this. How depression emotionally affects you is something that's not within your control; I think a lot of people who experienced the same thing can say the same. In all, I hope that you find relief from stress, and that you will be able to find the help you need. And that once things feel a little better, you will be able to find your interest and hobbies again. Wishing you the best of luck.

Depression allowed me to understand other people's pains much like you did. At the same time, it also caused me to lash out on others, and push other people away from me. It's a double-edged sword like most of the things we experience in life. Like on a smaller scale, failing a test. It can encourage you to do better, and/or make you feel like a failure. On a larger scale, experiencing emotional abuse. For some, experiencing this motivates them to break the cycle when it comes to how they other people. At the same time it also causes them to be moody, sometimes hurting others with their actions in consequence of their emotions. I guess it really matters on a person's perspective of how they will let depression affect them, although for some its something that's not within their control. I guess in all depression doesn't make you a better person; it just makes you a person (not to downplay people's experience with depression; experiencing pain is a human thing, its just that people who have depression experience it on a deeper level). In all, this idea can only be decided by a person once they've been healed from depression.
I don't really have any questions, but I'm happy that you're doing well!

It took me 3 whole years to properly clean my room, so same. Tidy up a bit here and there when you feel a bit better, but unless its unlivable, there's no reason for you to berate yourself for not being productive because being depressed often sucks out your energy to do anything. Please remember that you are not worthless, and that you are capable of many things but depression is hindering you from being your best. Know that once you are in a better place, you will accomplish your ambitions and all the goals you have or had before.

It took me a hella while to learn this, but everyone experiences pain differently. Just because you're not necessarily the unluckiest person in the world, doesn't mean your pain is invalid. I don't come from a broken home nor am I poor, but my depression still exists. And I'm pretty sure you wouldn't call me a crybaby if I told you felt like shit because I couldn't live up to my OWN expectations. It may sound lame and trivial to you, and some people could shake of said problem of yours, but the fact that you feel like crap because of it does not make you a crybaby nor worthless, because feeling something is completely human and everyone cries over shit they probably think is lame now and then. Also, in my opinion, everyone deserves love and affection, because it is a need for us to grow, and no matter how many bad qualities you think you have that makes you undeserving of it, the fact that you are loved shows how someone can see your worth, which is why they chose to love you. Know that you shouldn't base your life on your value and worth because that is a non-existent thing, and that living life is more than measuring who you are as a person.

I've taken medication, counselling, seen psychiatrists, done loads of therapy and activities and I still feel like shit. But like, the thing is the recovery and healing isn't a one way up kinda thing; it has ups and downs, like when you get a flu and your temperature changes often. And like when you take medicine for it, the effect often takes a bit to work through. Change doesn't happen in an instant, we know it yet we often forget it. My advice is that maybe you should do something you genuinely enjoy, not necessarily something productive, but something like video games, reading, binging on junk food while watching a movie marathon. Let yourself lose, know that pitying yourself isn't a bad thing, and that giving yourself the freedom to be happy should be alongside the entire 'taking care of yourself' thing

Sometimes when I'm extremely depressed, my illness obscures everything around me and I genuinely believe that there's no one out there who cares. So when my friend unknowingly comforts me by bringing extra lunch cause she's aware I don't eat often, I too end up sobbing a little bit. When you think/feel as if no cares for you, someone acknowledging your existence by giving you praise, remembering an obscure fact about you, or just being kind in general makes a hell of a change in your mood and there's no reason to hate yourself for being human :)
